title: Tape change; Baptiste O'Quinn and the color line in hiring
summary: After a reel change Allen asks about Baptiste O'Quinn; Laine says he stopped hiring him on learning he was Black, in a racist account.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yes, I knew him. Did you hear him play much? Yes, I heard him play. Papa, can I talk a while? Yeah. Because the tape's about to run out, and I want to do some talking now while I'm changing the tapes. Okay. Okay. I don't know what I'm going to say, but I'll talk. Yeah, this is a second reel on Papa Lane. I got it going now. It's April the 25th, 1964. Who was Baptiste O'Quinn? I got to get over there, Papa. You can't hear me. Who was Baptiste O'Quinn? Baptiste O'Quinn? Yeah.
Well, I wouldn't know. I wouldn't know who he was, but when I found out he was a nigger, that's when I stopped hiring him.

Yeah. When I found out he was a colored boy, I stopped hiring him. I never knew he was colored, but he married a white woman. He's married to a white lady. And I never knew it. But I didn't know that he was a colored boy. Never knew it. One fine day, I passed on Osterlein Street, where he lived. And I saw his daddy. And that was a no.
What did he play? What instrument? Ask him what instrument.
Violin and an alto. An alto. An alto.
